Event/Bulletin Title: Punjab Region Risk Event – Supplier Sites Outside the Impact Area Mapped for Impact Confirmation (Eaton/Ford)
Automation Opportunity: Geographic validation of supplier site geocodes against the event impact polygon before impact-confirmation requests are issued, so sites outside the affected region cannot be attached to an event
Comments: One incident reported by two customers on consecutive days, merged from Jira EAO-35 (Eaton, 07-Sep, Open) and EAO-36 (Ford, 08-Sep, Open). Eaton queried why four Tier 1 suppliers including a logistics partner were mapped to a Punjab risk event when their CDIF lists only Kumar Exports in Punjab, with Bhavani Industries (Maharashtra) and MT Autocraft (Himachal Pradesh) also attached and Tier 2 mappings reaching LOROM Industrial (Taipei) and DB Schenker (Barcelona). Ford separately reported that a Punjab power-cut WarRoom sent an impact-confirmation request to SMI AMTEK CRANKSHAFT in Dharuhera, Haryana, and that SNAP shows no active direct Tier 1 suppliers in Punjab at all, generating wasted supplier outreach. The geofence polygon over the affected region was correct and supplier selection is system-driven, so the probable cause is incorrect geocoding of supplier site coordinates rather than an operator or polygon error. Ford requested RCA, immediate corrective action and preventive corrective action. Number of Customers is 2; see the customer exposure table for the per-customer split.

Event/Bulletin Title: Record Heavy Rain in Yokkaichi City, Japan – No EventWatch Notification (Sandisk)
Automation Opportunity: Timeliness monitoring that flags a region already producing captured stories where a related event has not been published within the reporting window
Comments: Staged from Jira EAO-37 (Open). Sandisk was alerted internally to record heavy rain in Yokkaichi city, Japan and could find no news item or WarRoom for it, despite having loaded their own Yokkaichi sites as suppliers. The customer supplied no public source. CS verified the Sandisk org and then the database across all customer orgs and found no evidence the notification was ever generated, so the event did not enter the system at all rather than being filtered out. RCA requested.
RCA Details: Not a coverage gap and not a Not Impactful call. The news was in the public domain and other Japan flooding stories were being captured on the analyst portal at the time; this one was delayed in reporting and only published on 09-Sep-2026, after the customer had raised the query on 08-Sep. Sandisk's complaint is that it never reached the notified section of their portal, which is the downstream effect of the reporting delay rather than a separate visibility defect.

Event/Bulletin Title: Vertiv Acquires UtilityInnovation Group – Supplier Notification and Medium Risk Classification Queried (Eaton)
Automation Opportunity: Automated enforcement of the M&A notification threshold so acquiring-side suppliers are excluded from impact-confirmation requests, plus a documented basis for the risk classification
Comments: Staged from Jira EAO-38 (Open). Eaton queried WarRoom 37485945, 'Vertiv Acquires UtilityInnovation Group' (event date 08-Sep-2026, closed, severity Low). Two questions: why a Supplier Impact Confirmation Request was issued when the supplier is the acquiring party, which the latest Resilinc event-threshold guidance says does not require supplier notification; and why the event was classified Medium risk. The customer wants to know whether scenarios are being missed. A written explanation covering both was requested rather than an RCA.
RCA Details: Not a defect. The Supplier Impact Confirmation was issued in line with one of the customers mapped to that supplier, whose settings called for it, so the request was correct for that account even though Eaton reads the M&A threshold as excluding an acquiring supplier. The answer to Eaton is an explanation of how supplier notification follows each mapped customer's own configuration, plus the basis for the risk grade.
